html:
SMTO-EXE-0121 — SMTO stopped waiting before the download finished

GUID: ee7562e4-1be1-57ed-b032-5a6c7b2f840e
Slug: browser-download-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO waited for a file to download, but the wait ended before it saw the download finish. The file may still be downloading or may already be done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "List your browser downloads and tell me the status of the file." Don't ask it to click Download again. The first download may still be running or already finished, and a second click could make a duplicate.
  2. If the file has finished, ask SMTO to save that download to the task's files. The finished file only becomes available to you once SMTO saves it from the browser.
  3. If it is still downloading, ask SMTO to keep waiting for that same download, up to one minute at a time. Large files can take longer than SMTO's default wait of about 10 seconds.
  4. Don't let SMTO close its browser until the file is saved. Closing the browser throws away downloads that haven't been saved yet.

What success looks like

  • The download shows as completed, and the file appears in the task's files.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and website, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't start the download again just because the wait ended.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's wait_for_download hit its time limit before the download reached a final state; the download itself may still be running or may have finished.

What this means

  • SMTO stopped waiting for a terminal download result. The download may still be running or may have completed after the wait ended. Inspect the existing download record before issuing another trigger; this timeout alone cannot establish the original download outcome.

Why this can happen

  • The existing download did not become observably terminal within the wait limit. The browser’s current download record can distinguish running, completed and failed states.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing download ID with browser.downloads. If it is still running, observe that download; if completed, use its recorded artifact; if failed, inspect its recorded failure before choosing another action.

How to fix it

  • BrowserService._execute raised download_timeout when the wait_for_download deadline (timeout_ms, default 10 s, max 60 s) expired; this does not show the download was never triggered. Call browser.downloads, and for the existing download_id call wait_for_download with download_id (and as_artifact=true to export it) instead of clicking the download trigger again. Export before stopping the session, since stopping releases browser downloads.
  • Inspect the existing download with browser.downloads and its saved receipt before triggering anything again. Use the completed artifact if present, or keep observing the same running download.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect browser.downloads. Wait for the existing download ID rather than clicking the download trigger again.

How to verify the fix

  • The same download ID has a terminal status, and a completed download identifies its artifact.

What not to do

  • Do not click Download again merely because the wait timed out.

Technical notes

  • The wait_for_download observer exceeded its deadline. A wait timeout does not show that the original download was never triggered.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
